Each agent identity must anchor its first action to a recently published block that only exists during a random gale window announced after the fact; idle pre-registered identities miss it. Agents then pay a per-action nectar fee proportional to identity age divided by witnessed peer interactions, so fresh masks incur maximum cost. An attacker sustaining N identities must either keep them continuously active or pay escalating fees, making coordination measurably expensive.
